summary: Aberdeen’s Labour council gave Nelson Mandela the freedom of the city, prompting MoD concerns over a possible Gordon Highlanders performance and leading the MoD to conclude there should be no dancing.
Nelson Mandela was released from Victor Verster prison in Paarl, near Cape Town, after 27 years in prison.
Nelson Mandela was released.

Nelson Mandela was prevented from meeting Margaret Thatcher in London in mid-April 1990 after his appointments secretary Zwelakhe Sisulu persuaded the ANC leadership to veto the meeting, according to a confidential US embassy cable.
Tony Blair’s visit to South Africa aims to establish a rapport with Thabo Mbeki, who is expected to replace Nelson Mandela when Mandela retires in the spring.
F.W. de Klerk’s memoirs reveal a bitter personal feud with Nelson Mandela, including Mandela’s 1991 Codesa attack and disputes over Nobel Prize and presidential residences.
South African President Nelson Mandela named June 2 as the date for the election to choose his successor.

Nelson Mandela ruled out a future as a roving mediator resolving international conflicts, citing his experience dealing with the British government over the Lockerbie bombing suspects, and reiterated his determination to retire into obscurity.
Nelson Mandela's lawyers dismissed allegations that he accepted a kickback for fixing an oil deal, saying the cheques were unsolicited contributions to his children's fund.

A biography of Nelson Mandela by Anthony Sampson is reviewed as South Africa's second democratic elections approach and Mandela retires, with the review noting that critical appraisal of Mandela is muted and a definitive biography has yet to be written.
Nelson Mandela voted in South Africa's national election, which was expected to send him into retirement with a landslide for his ruling party.
Poet laureate Andrew Motion writes a verse to mark Nelson Mandela's retirement, which he will inscribe in a House of Commons tribute book.

The South African government planned new monuments and heritage sites, including several associated with Nelson Mandela, to recognize anti-apartheid heroes and reduce colonial and Afrikaner dominance in public symbols.
Nelson Mandela returned home to find his retirement garden in Qunu transformed by the BBC1 series Ground Force.
Former South African foreign minister Pik Botha describes Nelson Mandela as a better leader than FW de Klerk and plans to join the ruling African National Congress.
Nelson Mandela marks the 10th anniversary of his release from apartheid jails at a ceremony at his birthplace in rural Transkei.

Nelson Mandela angrily denied claims from a forthcoming book that he was recruited as an MI6 “agent of influence” and had visited MI6 headquarters, saying he never visited the headquarters of any intelligence service.

Nelson Mandela, on his first visit to Britain since retiring as South African president, accuses Britain and America of acting as "policemen of the world" by ignoring the UN and launching military actions against Iraq and Kosovo.
A paperback edition of Anthony Sampson’s authorized biography of Nelson Mandela is reviewed as the paperback of the week.

The British Library restores a 1964 recording of Nelson Mandela’s “prepared to die” speech from the Rivonia trial, and Mandela says he knew nothing about the tapes’ existence and is interested to hear them for the first time.
Nelson Mandela was freed from prison after 27 years on 11 February 1990.
A project is unveiled to erect a 9 ft bronze statue of Nelson Mandela in Trafalgar Square, London, near South Africa House.
A letter proposes a statue of Nelson Mandela in Trafalgar Square as a historical counterpoint to the statue of Jan Christiaan Smuts, commemorating the end of apartheid.

Nelson Mandela said he will present Tony Blair with fresh evidence supposedly clearing the Libyan intelligence officer jailed for the Lockerbie bombing, following a meeting with Muammar Gadafy and the family of Abdel Basset Ali al-Megrahi in Tripoli.
Nelson Mandela is visiting Britain this weekend for a Freedom Day concert in Trafalgar Square.
Nelson Mandela is to host a free concert in London's Trafalgar Square to thank the British people for their stand against apartheid.
Nelson Mandela visited Leeds to open a £12m improvement of Mandela Gardens, thanking local people for their support during his 27 years in prison.
Cape Town's mayor lost his job for his role in fabricating public petitions in favour of renaming two city streets after Nelson Mandela and FW de Klerk.
Nelson Mandela is scheduled to give a lecture at the University of Oxford when its newest lecture theatre, in the Saïd business school, is named in his honour.
Nelson Mandela plans to visit Abdel Baset al-Megrahi, the Libyan convicted of the Lockerbie bombing, in Barlinnie prison, Glasgow, to check on his welfare.
Nelson Mandela visits Athens to support the Greek campaign for an Olympic truce during the 2004 games.
Percy Yutar, the lawyer who prosecuted Nelson Mandela in the 1964 Rivonia trial, dies at age 90.

Nelson Mandela's former prison house at Victor Verster, where he spent his last 14 months of captivity, has been designated a national heritage site and turned into a museum, expected to open to visitors within the next few weeks.
A BBC documentary about Nelson Mandela, titled "Mandela: The Living Legend," is reviewed, describing his post-retirement schedule, fundraising for his foundation, and interactions with world leaders.

The final report of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission found that former President FW de Klerk failed to make full disclosure about human rights violations, while Nelson Mandela was noted for establishing the commission in July 1995.
Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, former wife of Nelson Mandela, was sentenced to four years in prison for fraud and theft.
Westminster council's public arts advisory panel rejected a proposal to place a statue of Nelson Mandela on the north terrace of Trafalgar Square, judging it aesthetically inappropriate.

Westminster City Council's public arts committee stated its opposition to an application for a statue of Nelson Mandela on Trafalgar Square, despite widespread support and Mandela's own thanks to the people of London for the idea.
Nelson Mandela launched the Mandela-Rhodes Foundation in Westminster Hall, receiving tributes from Bill Clinton and Tony Blair.
Nelson Mandela unveiled a blue plaque in London at the former home of anti-apartheid activists Joe Slovo and Ruth First, praising them as great comrades.
Nelson Mandela turned 85, prompting nationwide celebrations in South Africa and renewed public debate about the country's future after his death.
President Thabo Mbeki inaugurated South Africa's new constitutional court in a rebuilt 100-year-old prison where Nelson Mandela, Mahatma Gandhi, and captured Boer War generals were once detained.
Nelson Mandela is reported to be beginning a gradual withdrawal from public life due to health concerns and fatigue, though the Nelson Mandela Foundation denies he will withdraw completely.
Nelson Mandela gave a farewell speech to South Africa's parliament, warning that HIV/AIDS threatened the country's future and criticizing the US and Britain over the Iraq war.
Former South African President Nelson Mandela announced he was retiring from public life to spend time with his family and in quiet reflection.
Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, former wife of Nelson Mandela, escaped jail when a four-year theft sentence was overturned on appeal, though fraud convictions were upheld.

Nelson Mandela’s grandson Mandla Mandela said at his father Makgatho’s funeral that his mother Zondi had also died of AIDS last year, following Nelson Mandela’s earlier announcement that Makgatho died of AIDS-related complications.
Nelson Mandela backs Gordon Brown's "Marshall plan" for Africa and says he will travel to London in February to lobby a meeting of G7 finance ministers.
Nelson Mandela appeared at Trafalgar Square in support of the Make Poverty History campaign, calling on rich nations to give Africa a better deal on trade, debt and aid.
Nelson Mandela came out of retirement to speak at a rally in Trafalgar Square, calling on rich nations to act on poverty and inequality.
Nelson Mandela appeared at a Make Poverty History rally in Trafalgar Square, where he met schoolchildren and spoke about the need to end poverty and provide education for all children.
Anti-apartheid campaigner Raymond Mhlaba, a member of the Rivonia group with Nelson Mandela, died aged 85.
Nelson Mandela officially endorsed London's bid to host the 2012 Olympic Games.
London mayor Ken Livingstone accuses Westminster council of double standards over the location of a Nelson Mandela statue in Trafalgar Square, as a public inquiry into the decision continues.
Nelson Mandela launched the first edition of a series of comic books about his life aimed at encouraging young South Africans to read.

Salford city council granted Nelson Mandela the freedom of the city, with a representative from the South African high commission accepting the award on his behalf at a ceremony at the Lowry arts centre.
Nelson Mandela met with schoolchildren and Gordon Brown in Maputo, Mozambique, as part of the Global Campaign for Education to call for free education for all children.
South Africa celebrates Nelson Mandela's 88th birthday as he remains publicly silent on political issues.
David Cameron said that Nelson Mandela was not a terrorist.
Nelson Mandela, Tony Blair, and Bill Clinton back a $5m award initiative for African rulers, formally launched in London by Mo Ibrahim's foundation.
A decision was agreed to place a statue of Nelson Mandela in Parliament Square, with the statue to be unveiled later in 2007.
A Westminster council planning committee approved a statue of Nelson Mandela to be placed in Parliament Square in London, ending a five-year dispute over its location.

Former South African President FW de Klerk reflects that Nelson Mandela's 1964 speech was received with indifference by the apartheid government, but that Mandela survived 27 years in prison to lead South Africa to non-racial democracy, though aspects of his vision remain unfulfilled.

Nelson Mandela marked his 89th birthday with the launch of the Elders, a group of world-renowned figures including former US president Jimmy Carter, former UN secretary general Kofi Annan, and former archbishop of Cape Town Desmond Tutu, to tackle global crises.

A nine-foot bronze statue of Nelson Mandela was unveiled in Parliament Square, London, at a ceremony attended by Mandela, his wife Graca Machel, London mayor Ken Livingstone, and prime minister Gordon Brown.
In an interview, Desmond Tutu discusses Nelson Mandela's role in the negotiations that ended apartheid and his 1996 nomination of Tutu to chair the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.
A radio program recalls that Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika was sung at Nelson Mandela's 1994 inauguration as South Africa's first democratic president.
Nelson Mandela arrived in London for a week of events celebrating his 90th birthday.
The US government removed Nelson Mandela and the African National Congress from its terror watch list, a move Condoleezza Rice called correcting an "embarrassing" absurdity.
Nelson Mandela attended a formal celebration of his 90th birthday at his home in Qunu, Eastern Cape, with 500 guests and a Xhosa choir.
A statue of Nelson Mandela is unveiled at Drakenstein prison, where he completed his sentence.
Nelson Mandela's office denies speculation that he no longer supports the African National Congress, calling the assumption "completely erroneous."
Nelson Mandela made a rare appearance at an ANC rally in the Eastern Cape to support Jacob Zuma, though he did not speak.
Nelson Mandela made a surprise appearance at the African National Congress's final campaign rally before the elections in Johannesburg.
Nelson Mandela reports receiving a telegram from a white Cape Town housewife criticizing his speech after his release from 27 years as a political prisoner as very boring.
Nelson Mandela's foundation announces he will withdraw almost entirely from public life to spend more time with his family, denying rumours that he is extremely ill.
Thousands gather near Cape Town to celebrate the 20th anniversary of Nelson Mandela's release from prison, with Winnie Madikizela-Mandela leading a commemorative march.
South African parliament commemorates the 20th anniversary of Nelson Mandela's release from prison, with Mandela present in the chamber.

Veterans of South Africa's anti-apartheid struggle retraced Nelson Mandela's final steps as a political prisoner to commemorate the 20th anniversary of his release, though Mandela himself did not appear.

Nelson Mandela's ex-wife Winnie Madikizela-Mandela denies giving a newspaper interview in which she was quoted criticising Mandela over his decision to accept the 1993 Nobel peace prize alongside FW de Klerk.
Nelson Mandela is expected to make a brief appearance at the World Cup opening ceremony before South Africa play Mexico.
Nelson Mandela attends the funeral of his great-granddaughter Zenani, who was killed in a car crash on the eve of the World Cup.
Nelson Mandela attended the World Cup closing ceremony in South Africa, receiving a rapturous reception from fans.
A review of Nelson Mandela's book Conversations with Myself is published, describing it as a literary album of diaries, letters, and recordings that offers an intimate portrait of Mandela.
Cape Town is set to name a street Nelson Mandela Boulevard, replacing Eastern Boulevard, making it one of the last major cities to honor Mandela with a street name.

Nelson Mandela met Michelle Obama and her daughters Malia and Sasha at the Nelson Mandela Foundation in Johannesburg, his first public appearance since being released from hospital in January after an acute respiratory infection.

Plans were said to be afoot for David Cameron to pay an Eastern Cape birthday visit to Nelson Mandela on Nelson Mandela Day, but the visit did not take place as Cameron's Africa trip was cut short by the phone-hacking scandal.
Nelson Mandela approved a $20m six-hour TV mini-series about his life, due to go into production later in 2012.
Former South African President Nelson Mandela was admitted to hospital for treatment of a long-standing abdominal complaint and was reported fine and fully conscious.
Nelson Mandela was discharged from a Pretoria hospital and returned to his home in Johannesburg after undergoing a diagnostic laparoscopy for an abdominal complaint.
Winnie Madikizela-Mandela allegedly sent a leaked email accusing the ANC of shabby treatment of the Mandela family and criticizing the exploitation of Nelson Mandela's birthday.
President Jacob Zuma said after a Christmas Day visit that Nelson Mandela was in good spirits and looking much better while being treated in a Pretoria hospital for a lung infection and gallstones.
Nelson Mandela was discharged from hospital after 19 days of treatment for a lung infection and gallstones, and will undergo home-based high care at his Johannesburg home.
The Mandela 27 project launches a video game, website, and mobile replicas of Nelson Mandela's Robben Island prison cell to teach young people about apartheid history.
Nelson Mandela is admitted to hospital just before midnight for treatment of a recurring lung infection.
Nelson Mandela was discharged from hospital after being treated for pneumonia for more than a week.
Former South African President Nelson Mandela was taken to a Pretoria hospital due to a recurrence of a lung infection, in serious but stable condition.
Former South African President Nelson Mandela's health deteriorated from serious to critical.
A 1990 "Welcome Mandela" plaque was presented to the South African high commission and will be displayed permanently in Brent's new civic centre in Wembley.
South African officials say Nelson Mandela's condition has improved and he remains critical but is now stable.
Barack Obama calls Nelson Mandela "a hero for the world" while Mandela remains critically ill.
South Africa and the world celebrated Nelson Mandela's 95th birthday while he remained hospitalized in Pretoria, with officials reporting his condition was steadily improving.
The Robert J. Dole Institute of Politics announces it will honor Nelson Mandela with the Bob Dole leadership prize, which includes a $25,000 cash reward.

Director John Irvin announces a drama-documentary, Mandela's Gun, chronicling Nelson Mandela's years as a guerrilla freedom fighter, which will feature a South African actor, Tumisho Masha, as Mandela.
South African President Jacob Zuma announced that Nelson Mandela will be accorded a state funeral and ordered all national flags to be lowered to half-mast until after the funeral.
Nelson Mandela died at the age of 95.
Following Nelson Mandela's death, an article reflects on his significance to black Britain, including his moral authority and intervention in the Stephen Lawrence murder case.
World leaders prepare to converge on South Africa for Nelson Mandela's funeral, with a memorial service planned for 2013-12-10 at Johannesburg's Soccer City stadium and burial to take place in Qunu.
Nelson Mandela, the last of a great generation of freedom fighters who guided South Africa's liberation struggle, has died.
Nelson Mandela's family released their first statement since his death, mourning the loss of "a great man, a son of the soil" and "the pillar of the royal Mandela family."
Nelson Mandela is remembered as a world statesman who made time for everyone, following his death.
South Africans hold a national day of prayer to remember Nelson Mandela following his death on 2013-12-05.
Nelson Mandela's preserved office at the Nelson Mandela Centre of Memory in Johannesburg became a point of pilgrimage as visitors viewed it following his death.
Civil rights activist Jesse Jackson reflects on Nelson Mandela’s release from prison in Cape Town and his legacy following Mandela’s death.
UK Parliament held tributes to Nelson Mandela following his death, with MPs including David Cameron and Ed Miliband offering contrition and praise.

A national memorial service is held in Johannesburg for Nelson Mandela, who died the previous week aged 95, with nearly a hundred heads of state attending and Barack Obama delivering a keynote address.
Nelson Mandela lies in state at the Union Buildings in Pretoria, drawing thousands of South Africans to queue and view his casket.
A week of tributes and beatification of Nelson Mandela by Western figures is criticized as hypocritical, highlighting his armed struggle, socialism, and opposition to US and British wars.
Prince Charles is to attend Nelson Mandela's state funeral in Qunu on behalf of the Queen, while David Cameron will attend the public memorial service in Johannesburg on 2013-12-10.
Newly released Downing Street files show Margaret Thatcher did not raise Nelson Mandela's case during her 1984 Chequers meeting with PW Botha, casting doubt on claims she pressured for his release.

The 50th anniversary of Nelson Mandela's "I am prepared to die" speech from the dock during the Rivonia trial is marked, amid calls to preserve the neglected holding cell beneath the Pretoria courtroom where he and fellow accused were held.

Jerry Dammers is to be honoured in South Africa with the Order of the Companions of OR Tambo for his anti-apartheid song Free Nelson Mandela, during Freedom Day events marking the 20th anniversary of South Africa's first democratic elections in which Mandela was elected president.
As the 25th anniversary of Nelson Mandela’s release from prison is marked, FW de Klerk’s legacy is contested, including anger over Cape Town’s decision to rename Table Bay Boulevard after De Klerk.
A musical/opera titled "Mandela Trilogy" depicting Nelson Mandela's life story, with over 60 performers, opened at the Royal Festival Hall in London.
A proposed statue of Nelson Mandela is the subject of a public debate, with critics questioning the sculptor's work and the mayor's ambition for the monument.
Nelson Mandela was sentenced to life in 1964.
Nelson Mandela's 1996 visit to Britain is referenced as a testimony to courage, contrasted with Jacob Zuma's later state visit.
A biography of Nelson Mandela by Anthony Sampson is reviewed, detailing his life, imprisonment, and role in ending apartheid.
